fields.rationale: Bodies are grouped by the type of institutional home: a dedicated board for that single profession, a board shared across related professions, a public health department, a catch-all professional/occupational licensing agency, a labor and industry department, a consumer protection body, an education department, or another executive-branch agency that fits none of the above.

Bodies are bucketed by the type of regulatory structure they represent — a dedicated single-profession board, a board shared across related trades or professions, a broad medical/healing-arts board covering multiple clinical professions, a state health department, a general professional-licensing or commerce agency, a state education department, or another state agency — regardless of which specific profession they regulate.

Each raw value was grouped by the functional type of the parent department — whether it primarily serves consumer/business oversight, public health, labor/workforce, dedicated licensing administration, commerce/economic development, the Secretary of State's office, or falls into a residual category.

Values are bucketed by the type of accrediting authority named: a national body dedicated to that profession's discipline, a regional or institutional higher-education accreditor, an explicit federal reference (U.S. Department of Education or CHEA), a licensing/regulatory board exercising discretion over school approval, a state-level agency or state board, or a trade/apprenticeship oversight body.

Values are grouped by the dominant mechanism that gates recognition: whether the core requirement is a standards-equivalency finding, a minimum years-in-practice rule, participation in a formal interstate compact, passing or having passed an equivalent exam, a bilateral mutual-reciprocity agreement between states, a comprehensive multi-factor review combining several independent criteria, or a purely administrative/fee-only path.
